chunks: My father narrated (may God be pleased with him) who said: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated from Ayyub ibn Nuh, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from Sa'd ibn Abi Khalaf, from Najm, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

He said to me: 'O Najm! All of you are in Paradise with us, except that how awkward it is for a man from among you to enter Paradise having had his honor stripped away and his private parts exposed.' I said to him: 'May I be your ransom, is this indeed going to happen?' He said: 'Yes, if he has not guarded his private parts and his stomach.'
ai.seo_question: What causes a believer to enter Paradise with lost honor according to Imam al-Baqir?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Khisal*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies that entry into Paradise is not guaranteed by mere affiliation, but requires the preservation of one's spiritual and physical honor. The specific mention of guarding the 'private parts and stomach' highlights the Shia emphasis on *haya* (modesty) and *taqwa* (God-consciousness) in regulating the two primary gates of desire: sexual chastity and dietary discipline. This serves as a reminder that negligence in these areas can lead to a state of spiritual exposure even within the bliss of the afterlife.
